docs.title: FOSS United Platform
docs.text:
The FOSS United Platform is an open source community management platform built using the Frappe Framework. It serves as the central hub for all FOSS United activities, including event organization, community collaboration, grant tracking, and more.

This platform is part of a larger mission to foster a vibrant Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) ecosystem in India. Whether you're a developer, enthusiast, educator, or industry partner, you're invited to explore, contribute, and grow with the community.

Together, we're building a culture of openness, collaboration, and innovation through FOSS.

docs.title: What's on the Platform
docs.text:
• User Profiles Showcase your contributions, maintain a portfolio, and manage your activities through a personal dashboard.

  • FOSS Communities & Clubs Join or manage local FOSS communities across India.

  • Event Hosting Organize and participate in community events.

  • Grants and Initiatives Track and apply for community grants, explore ongoing initiatives.

See more on what we do here.

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text:
• Backend: Python with Frappe Framework
  • Frontend: HTML/CSS, Vue.js, Bootstrap v4, TailwindCSS
  • Database: MariaDB
  • Caching: Redis

FOSS United relies on a variety of self-hosted services, which you can find listed here

docs.title: Getting Involved
docs.text:
The FOSS United Platform is open to contributions, code, content, and community. You can:

  • Report issues or suggest features on GitHub
  • Join local meetups or events
  • Contribute to this documentation
  • Help onboard new community members

docs.title: Architecture of the Platform
docs.text:
The FOSS United Platform is built using the Frappe framework. In case you're not already aware, applications that use the Frappe framework are built around DocTypes. For example, the FOSSUserProfile, which powers the Profile, is a DocType. The names of a few DocTypes that are fundamental to the Platform can be found in fossunited.doctype_ids.

If you are unfamiliar with Entity relationship diagrams or if you need a refresher, you could refer to the wiki section on the Crow's foot notation, or this explainer from freecodecamp

docs.title: Architecture Diagram
docs.text:
Note: Not all features or systems in this diagram are actually used, as the diagram also includes components of what Frappe uses underneath the hood.

graph TD;

    U[User Browser] <--> N[nginx];
    U <--> V[VueJS Dashboard];

    Admin[Admin Browser] <--> D[Desk: SPA Custom JS];

    N <--> C[Application Server: Gunicorn & Werkzeug];

    C <--> D;
    C <--> E[Socket.io Server: Node & Redis];
    C <--> F[Jinja Templating Engine];
    C <--> G[Background Workers: Python RQ];
    C <--> H[MariaDB];
    C <--> I[Redis Cache];
    C <--> J[Amazon S3: File Storage];

    G <--> I;
    G <--> H;

docs.title: RSVP to an event
docs.text: Events such as monthly meetups usually require attendees to RSVP for the event. This helps the event organizers plan accordingly e.g. purchase snacks and beverages.

docs.title: RSVP-ing to an event
docs.text:
Note: RSVP-ing to an event does not require you to have a Profile.

  • Visit the RSVP tab for the event and click on the "RSVP for the event" green button

  • Complete the form with the necessary information. Please note that if you are logged in, the Platform will auto-fill some of the information i.e. the Full Name and Email fields.
  • Also it lets you edit your RSVP.
  • You can also opt-in to "Subscribing" to Chapter mailing group from the organizing community to stay updated. Note: You can edit RSVP and opt-out from email group anytime.

  • You should receive an email from FOSS United after you successfully submit the form.

Note: Please note that some of the events might need additional information from the participants e.g. mobile phone numbers. This is because some of the venue partners where the meetups are organized might require the attendees to provide their mobile phone numbers to enter the building or office premises.

docs.title: Updating your RSVP
docs.text:
If you are unable to attend an event that you previously RSVP'ed to, we request you to update the status of your RSVP. Like we mentioned earlier, the RSVP information is used by the organizers to make decisions about the meetup e.g. tea/coffee and snacks ordered for the event. Accurate RSVP information prevents wasting time, energy, money, and food.

  • Visit the RSVP tab of the event that you previously RSVP'ed to

  • You can click on "I can't attend the Event" to inform organizers that you won't attend.

  • You can also confirm to re-attend via same button as it changes to "I'll attend the Event!" and click "Update" to confirm the changes.

docs.title: Lead a FOSS Club
docs.text: Starting a FOSS Club on a college campus is a fantastic way to foster collaboration, innovation, and learning among students. FOSS United provides support and resources to help establish and grow FOSS Clubs. Here's a step-by-step guide to starting a FOSS Club in your college, with reference to FOSS United Clubs Program:

docs.title: 1. Gather Support:
docs.text:
• Seek support from faculty, administration, and fellow students.
  • Identify potential club members who share an interest in FOSS.

docs.title: 2. Form a Core Team:
docs.text:
• Assemble a team of enthusiastic students to lead and manage the club.
  • Assign roles and responsibilities, such as president, secretary, event coordinator, etc.

docs.title: 3. Register with FOSS United:
docs.text:
• Visit the FOSS United Clubs page and follow the registration process.
  • Gain access to resources, mentorship, and support provided by FOSS United.

docs.title: 4. Plan Activities and Events:
docs.text:
• Develop a calendar of regular meetings, workshops, hackathons, guest lectures, etc.
  • Collaborate with other clubs, organizations, and industry professionals.

docs.title: 5. Promote the Club:
docs.text:
• Create promotional materials, such as posters, flyers, and social media posts.
  • Organize introductory sessions to attract new members.

docs.title: 8. FOSS United Resources:
docs.text:
• Leverage the resources, tools, and platforms provided by FOSS United.
  • Engage with the FOSS United community for collaboration, mentorship, and knowledge sharing.

docs.title: 9. Foster a Collaborative Environment:
docs.text:
• Encourage members to contribute to open-source projects, participate in community events, and collaborate on innovative ideas.
  • Provide opportunities for skill development, networking, and career growth.

docs.title: 10. Monitor and Evaluate Progress:
docs.text:
• Regularly assess the club's progress towards its goals.
  • Gather feedback from members and make necessary adjustments.

docs.title: 11. Celebrate Success and Recognize Contributions:
docs.text:
• Acknowledge and celebrate achievements, contributions, and milestones.
  • Foster a sense of pride, belonging, and camaraderie among club members.

docs.title: 12. Stay Engaged with FOSS United:
docs.text:
• Maintain an active relationship with FOSS United for continued support, opportunities, and collaboration.

Starting a FOSS Club on a college campus is not just about coding and technology; it's about building a community that values collaboration, creativity, and social impact. By partnering with FOSS United, you can create a vibrant and dynamic club that empowers students to explore, innovate, and contribute to the global FOSS movement.

docs.title: Code contributions
docs.text:
Code contributions are usually what people refer to when they mean contributing to a FOSS project and we are glad to receive code contributions. If you are not sure where to start, we can recommend looking into the codebase to identify untested code and add unit tests. Testing ensures that the Platform is robust and works as expected and unit tests, integration tests, end-to-end tests, API tests, and more are welcome code contributions.

You could also look at the issue board to identify issues that you want to pick up. You don't have to ask us if you want to pick up an issue - as long as someone isn't already working on the issue, feel free to pick it up and open a Pull Request addressing the issue. The existing contributors usually assign themselves to an issue if they are actively working upon it.

Adding new features will likely require knowledge of the Frappe framework and if you don't have prior understanding of the framework, please dig in for a long and time-taking contribution process.

docs.title: Create event
docs.text:
• To schedule a new event, open the Community page where the event is being organized. Within the chapter, open the "Events" page and click on the "Create New Event" button as seen below.
  • Please provide the requested information in the form
Create event (…)
  • For monthly meetups, please use the following options
  • Please select "FOSS meetup" in the "Event Type" dropdown
  • Please use "FOSS Meetup {city name}" for the "Event Name" e.g. "FOSS Meetup Hyderabad"
  • Please use YYYY-MMM for the "Event Permalink" e.g. 2024-nov
  • Please use "Live" as the "Event Status"
  • Please select the start date & time and the end date & time for the event

After an event is created successfully, you should be able to see it in the "Manage Chapter" page.

docs.title: Update event
docs.text: Information about the event e.g. location of the event can be updated after the event is created. To update an event, open the event from the "Scheduled Events" section, update the necessary information, and click on the "Update Details" button.

docs.title: Conclude event
docs.text:
After an event has concluded, please update the "Event Status" from "Live" to "Concluded".

Note: The event will not be displayed under the "Past Events" section of the chapter page unless the "Event Status" is updated. We have observed events "disappear" from the public pages of chapters because the "Event Status" doesn't get updated and the events aren't displayed under "Upcoming Events" because the date & time for the event is in the past.

docs.title: Creating your Profile
docs.text:
• If you don't have a Profile, use the "login" button to initiate the process of creating a Profile
  • In the "login" page, use the "Sign up" button at the bottom to create a Profile
  • Please provide your name or an alias and an email address.

Note: Please note that it is not possible to change the email address associated with your Profile once it is created. The name or alias can be updated.

  • After completing the previous step, you should receive an email from us. The email will provide a link where you can set the password for the Profile.

Congratulations, you have created a FOSS United Profile.

docs.title: Delete personal data
docs.text: If you want us to delete your data that is saved on the FOSS United Foundation systems, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII), please submit your email address on the Delete Data page.

docs.title: FOSS United Platform – Developer Guide
docs.text:
The FOSS United Platform is developed and maintained by the FOSS United Foundation, with ongoing contributions from the community. Development takes place on GitHub.

Note: We welcome contributions from anyone. Join us by submitting issues, feature requests, or pull requests!

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: Recommended Frappe Version: v15+

docs.title: Recommended: Setup & Quick-start
docs.text:
Our recommended setup is via docker + frappe manager.

  • Install uv python manager and docker
  • uv init in a new directory
  • uv add frappe-manager
  • fm create foss.localhost
  • fm start choose site as it shows in menu
  • fm shell
  • bench get-app https://github.com/fossunited/fossunited.git
  • bench install-app fossunited - This will also install dashboard
  • Open foss.localhost in your browser and start exploring!
  • Dashboard page can be accessed via foss.localhost/dashboard

Note: Since dashboard is not running live, you'd need to bench build --apps fossunited for changes to update.

If you would prefer for manual method, please follow on below

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Set up your environment using the official Frappe installation guide.
  • If you encounter a MariaDB password issue, refer to this DigitalOcean guide to reset your root password.

If the kill command fails: 

ps aux | grep mysqld
sudo kill -9 <pid_of_mysqld> <pid_of_mysql_safe>

Ensure MySQL processes are fully stopped before restarting.

docs.title: 2. Setup Steps
docs.text:
# Create a new bench
bench init fossu-bench
cd fossu-bench

docs.title: Install Newsletter App
docs.text:
For frappe >= v16, the Newsletter module has been moved as an separate app. Install it before fossunited:

bench get-app https://github.com/frappe/newsletter
bench install-app newsletter

Related discussion: #1120

docs.title: Install FOSS United App
docs.text:
# Get the app
bench get-app https://github.com/fossunited/fossunited

# Create a new site
bench new-site test.localhost

# Install the app on the site
bench --site test.localhost install-app fossunited

# Start development server
bench start

To access the site in your browser, follow: Access Site via Browser

docs.title: NixOS Setup
docs.text: For those using NixOS, refer to this guide ==> Issue #1068 – NixOS Setup Guide to get going.

docs.title: FOSS United Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard is an admin UI for volunteers to manage activities across FOSS Clubs and City Chapters.

docs.title: Dashboard Setup
docs.text:
# Go to the dashboard directory
cd fossunited/dashboard

# Install dependencies
yarn install

docs.title: Required Configuration
docs.text:
In your site_config.json, add the following:

{
  "ignore_csrf": 1
}

docs.title: Run the Dashboard
docs.text:
yarn dev

The dashboard will be available at: ==> http://<your-site-name>:8080

docs.title: Pre-commit Hooks
docs.text:
To automatically run linters before commits:

pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install

Or use uv as an alternative Python package manager.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
One way to get involved with the project is to add and improve the documentation of the project. As the Community grows, the numbers of people who will be attending, the number of events, and the overall activity on the Platform is expected to grow. Clear and concise documentation ensures that the team is able to effectively communicate how the Platform should be used to the respective audience.

As you can see, a part of the documentation is meant for volunteers who actively manage events and such in the Community and the rest of the documentation is oriented meant for the rest of the Community for example, event participants. Please keep this in mind when adding or improving the documentation.

The documentation is built from Markdown files in the FOSS UNITED GitHub repository. The documentation is built using the MkDocs Python project and uses the Material for MkDocs and the MkDocs Material plugins. Every time changes are made in the develop branch to the docs/* folder on the Git repository, a GitHub Action gets triggered, which builds and pushes the documentation to the gh-pages branch, to be served using GitHub pages.

docs.title: Steps to build documentation locally
docs.text:
1. cd into docs directory

  2. Install MkDocs and plugins via pip or uv package manager

    uv add mkdocs mkdocs-material mkdocs-glightbox pre-commit

  3. Setup pre-commit hook

    pre-commit install

This enables spell and grammar check for docs content via vale.

  1. Build and serve the docs at http://127.0.0.1:8000/

    mkdocs serve

docs.title: Call for Proposals (CFP)
docs.text:
Sessions at FOSS United events are usually selected from a pool of proposals. After the event is announced, the event organizers usually request the Community to submit proposals e.g. talk proposals, workshop proposals. As the scheduled date of the event approaches, the organizers choose the final sessions from the submitted proposals with help from reviewers.

Note: Submitting a proposal to a FOSS United event does not require you to have a Profile.

docs.title: What to Propose?
docs.text:
FOSS United encourages a healthy mix of talks on

  • Broad computing/tech principles and concepts (e.g.: distributed computing, UI/UX stuff, queues, etc). This is great to intro first principles to a beginner audience.
  • People's personal projects and their journeys (technical + non-technical process and experience). No to-do projects, but decent, unique projects.
  • Fun technical stuff, like your hobby projects, projects which you tinkered on or even algorithms
  • Technical (language constructs, database, etc)
  • Incidental (design, philosophy, legalese, policy)

docs.title: What proposals are not acceptable?
docs.text:
• Proposals from organisations which seem to promote a certain product with overt commercial interest.
  • Proposals from influencers and content creators whose primary incentive seem to be promoting themselves or their social media profiles.

docs.title: Submit a Proposal
docs.text:
• In order to submit a proposal for a FOSS United event, visit the "Talk Proposal" tab on the event page and click on the "Submit a talk proposal" green button.
  • Please complete the requested details on the "Call for Proposal!" form. If you are logged in, the Platform will auto-fill some of the information on the form i.e. Full Name, Email. Before submitting, we request you to read the guidelines for proposals

Note: Please note some of the events might need additional information from the proposers.

CFP form (…)
  • You should receive an email from FOSS United after you successfully submit the form.

docs.title: Update a Proposal
docs.text:
You can access submitted proposals from the "Talk proposal" tab of the event. You might want to update the submitted proposal e.g. based on review comments from the event organizers. You can either use the "Edit CFP" button on this page or on the page that displays information about your proposal.

Talk proposal tab Proposal page
  • After updating the proposal as necessary, please click the "Update Talk Proposal" button to save the updates.

docs.title: Create RSVP form

Organizing and Participating in FOSS United Events
General Guidelines for Event Participants
docs.text:
• Set your phones and gadgets to Do Not Disturb mode to minimize disruptions.
  • Avoid discussions on topics that might offend others, including but not limited to politics, religion, and sensitive social issues.

docs.title: For Speakers

docs.title: Step-by-Step Guide to Organizing a FOSS United Event
docs.text: Organizing a meetup, conference, or workshop requires careful planning and teamwork. Use this roadmap to ensure your event is successful, inclusive, and aligned with FOSS United values.

docs.title: 1. Define Purpose and Scope
docs.text:
• Decide the theme, target audience, and objectives.
  • Determine the type of event: meetup, conference, workshop, or a combination.

docs.title: 2. Build a Core Team
docs.text:
• Gather a group of committed volunteers with diverse skills.
  • Assign clear roles: logistics, content curation, marketing, sponsorship management, etc.

docs.title: 3. Select Date and Venue
docs.text:
• Choose a date avoiding major holidays or conflicting events.
  • Pick a venue suitable for the expected crowd, ensuring accessibility, internet connectivity, and necessary facilities.

docs.title: 4. Plan Event Content
docs.text:
• Issue a Call for Proposals (CFP) inviting speakers, panelists, and workshop leaders.
  • Follow FOSS Conference Standards for speaker selection and content quality.
  • Use FOSS United platform to manage the website, CFP, schedule, and ticketing.

docs.title: 5. Secure Sponsorships
docs.text:
• Identify and approach potential sponsors.
  • Create sponsorship packages that align with FOSS community values.
  • Note: FOSS United offers financial support up to INR 25,000 for conferences and INR 4,000 for meetups.

docs.title: 6. Promote the Event
docs.text:
• Develop a marketing plan including social media, email newsletters, and community outreach.
  • Design appealing promotional materials using standard templates and branding.

docs.title: 7. Manage Registration and Ticketing
docs.text:
• Decide on ticket pricing, discounts, and free passes.
  • Set up a reliable online registration system.

docs.title: 8. Organize Logistics and Operations
docs.text:
• Coordinate travel and accommodation for speakers and guests.
  • Arrange catering, signage, audio-visual support, and other essentials.
  • Refer to the Task list for Conference Organizers for a comprehensive checklist.

docs.title: 9. Foster Community Engagement
docs.text:
• Keep community members involved through forums, social media, and interactive sessions.
  • Follow the FOSS Meetup Standards to maintain community-driven participation.

docs.title: 10. Execute On-the-Day Coordination
docs.text:
• Ensure smooth attendee registration and session flow.
  • Provide clear directions, assistance, and enforce safety protocols.
  • Enforce the Code of Conduct to maintain a respectful and inclusive environment.

docs.title: 11. Conduct Post-Event Follow-up
docs.text:
• Collect feedback from attendees, speakers, sponsors, and volunteers.
  • Share event highlights, photos, videos, and presentation materials publicly.
  • Publicly acknowledge and thank all contributors and participants.

docs.title: 12. Document and Report
docs.text:
• Keep detailed records of the event including financial.
  • Consult the Conference Organizer Handbook for best practices.

docs.title: 13. Reflect and Improve
docs.text:
• Review what went well and identify areas to improve.
  • Apply lessons learned to make future events even better.

Organizing a FOSS United event is a rewarding way to build community, foster collaboration, and celebrate open source. By following FOSS United standards and guidelines, you help create inclusive, impacting experiences that strengthen the FOSS ecosystem in India.

docs.title: What is FOSS
docs.text:
FOSS stands for "Free and Open Source Software." It refers to software that respects user freedom and is open source, meaning that the source code is made available to the public. Let's break down these two components:

  1. Free Software: The "free" stands for freedom (as in "free speech").

Free software respects users' freedom and community. It means that users have the freedom to run, copy, distribute, study, change, and improve the software. These freedoms are essential in enabling individuals and communities to make the software do what they want it to. Free software doesn't mean that the software is available at no cost (although it often is).

  1. Open Source Software: This means that the original source code of the software is made available without restrictions and may be redistributed and modified. It allows anyone to inspect, modify, and enhance the code, which can lead to a more transparent and community-driven development process.

FOSS promotes sharing, collaboration, community engagement, transparency, and the ability to customize software for individual or organizational needs. Some well-known examples of FOSS include the Linux operating system, the Apache HTTP Server, and the Mozilla Firefox web browser.

docs.title: Relationship between FOSS and FOSS United
FOSS (Free and Open Source Software)
docs.text:
1. Definition: FOSS stands for, Free and Open Source Software. It refers to software that is both free to use and open source, meaning that the source code is made available to the public.
  2. Nature: FOSS is a concept and a philosophy that promotes the freedom to run, copy, distribute, study, change, and improve software.
  3. Community: FOSS involves a global community of developers, users, and advocates who contribute to and benefit from open-source projects.
  4. Examples: Examples of FOSS include the Linux operating system, the Apache HTTP Server, and the Mozilla Firefox web browser.
  5. Impact: FOSS has transformed the software industry by encouraging collaboration, transparency, and community-driven development.

docs.title: FOSS United
docs.text:
1. Definition: FOSS United is a registered non-profit organization in India that is dedicated to fostering the growth and development of Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) projects and communities within the country.
  2. Nature: FOSS United is an organization with specific goals, initiatives, and activities aimed at promoting FOSS in various sectors including academia, social sector, industry, and government.
  3. Community: FOSS United has its own community of members, volunteers, industry partners, and supporters who actively contribute to the foundation's mission.
  4. Examples: Initiatives by FOSS United include the IndiaFOSS conference, FOSS Hack, and FOSS Pledge.
  5. Impact: FOSS United aims to revive the spirit of FOSS and hacking in India, create quality FOSS projects for the public good, and foster community-industry collaboration.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• FOSS is a broad term that encompasses the philosophy, principles, and practices related to Free and Open Source Software.
  • FOSS United is a specific organization that works to promote and support FOSS in India through various initiatives, events, and collaborations.

FOSS United aligns with the principles of FOSS and works to apply them in a localized context to make a positive impact on the FOSS landscape in India.

docs.title: Apply for FOSS Grant
docs.text: Applying for a FOSS Grant through FOSS United is a process that supports the development and use of Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) in India. Here's how you can apply:

docs.title: Eligibility Requirements
docs.text:
To be eligible for a grant, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Be an individual or organization working on a FOSS project in India.
  • Have a clear project plan that outlines the goals of the project and how the funds will be used.
  • Be able to demonstrate a need for funding.

docs.title: Funding Amounts
docs.text: The maximum amount of funding available for each grant is ₹6 lakh.

docs.title: Co-Sponsored Grants
docs.text: FOSS United allows organizations to co-sponsor specific FOSS projects and grants by providing a framework for fund disbursal and project management. Co-sponsored grants are executed with the combined approval of FOSS United and the grantee.

docs.title: Recent Grants
docs.text:
FOSS United has provided grants to various projects, including Rethink DNS, FireFiles, TinkerHub Foundation, Parseable, and more.

By offering these grants, FOSS United aims to foster the growth and development of the FOSS community in India, supporting projects that align with its mission and values.

Apply here

docs.title: Initiatives by FOSS United
docs.text:
FOSS United runs and supports a wide range of initiatives aimed at building a stronger Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) ecosystem in India.

  1. FOSS Grant: Provides financial grants to support promising FOSS projects, encouraging innovation, sustainability, and collaboration.

  2. Events: Organizes and sponsors events such as IndiaFOSS and FOSS Hack to bring together the community, foster collaboration, and celebrate FOSS culture.

  3. Public Policy Initiative: Conducts research and advocacy around FOSS-related public policies, aiming to influence government regulations and promote openness in technology governance.

  4. OASIS: A network of organizations committed to the belief that FOSS can empower social enterprises, citizen sector organizations, and communities to create scalable, positive impact.

  5. FOSS Clubs Program: Supports the creation and growth of FOSS Clubs in educational institutions to nurture the next generation of open source contributors.

  6. FOSS Pledge: A public declaration of support on Free and Open Source Software by individuals and organizations.

  7. Mon School: An educational platform offering courses that emphasize creativity, critical thinking, and foundational skills, especially for beginners and young learners.

  8. Job Board: Connects FOSS developers and contributors with organizations seeking talent, helping to bridge the gap between the FOSS ecosystem and the job market.

  9. FOSS Event Grant: Provides financial support to community-driven FOSS events.

These initiatives reflect FOSS United multifaceted approach to promoting Free and Open Source Software in India. By actively working across policy, education, community building, and infrastructure, FOSS United aims to play a key role in shaping the future of the open source movement in the country.

docs.title: Inclusive and Diversity
docs.text: We welcome everyone, irrespective of their background, expertise, or affiliations, to join, contribute, and flourish within our community.

docs.title: Collaboration and Participation
docs.text: Our ethos is rooted in open collaboration, shared knowledge, and collective problem-solving. We foster a milieu where every idea is valued, and every contribution is acknowledged.

docs.title: Respect and Understanding
docs.text: We are committed to nurturing a culture of respect and understanding. A comprehensive Code of Conduct will guide our interactions, ensuring a congenial and supportive environment akin to the respectful culture in the community.

docs.title: Transparency and Openness
docs.text: We uphold the principles of transparency and openness in all our endeavors. Our decision-making processes and discussions are open, inviting feedback and contributions from all community members.

docs.title: Continuous Learning and Improvement
docs.text: Our community is a crucible for continuous learning, sharing, and improvement. We promote a culture of curiosity and growth, encouraging every member to learn, share, and evolve.

docs.title: No Gate keeping
docs.text: We respect the diversity in choices of tools and technologies. Rather than imposing specific FOSS solutions, we aim to educate and suggest, allowing individuals to make informed decisions.

docs.title: User Privacy and Control
docs.text: Advocacy for software solutions that prioritize user privacy and control is fundamental to our principles. We strive to promote solutions that empower users rather than encroach upon their privacy.

docs.title: Open Standards
docs.text: Our advocacy extends to open standards ensuring interoperability, data portability, and a collaborative ecosystem. We believe open standards are pivotal for a cohesive and innovative ecosystem.

docs.title: Project Management
docs.text:
Work on the Platform is planned and executed using a GitHub project at the moment and known issues about the project are tracked using the GitHub issues board.

This is more or less reflected in Changelog.md in text format explaining the changes as monthly tech report from FOSS united foundation and platform. Updates are also be communicated in blog and forum post to keep the community informed.

The GitHub issues board organizes work in a clear workflow:

  • Issues that the Foundation is actively working on are placed in the "ToDo" column.
  • Issues planned for future prioritization, such as the next month, are placed in the "No Status" column.
  • When an issue is picked up for work, it is moved to the "In Progress" column and assigned to the responsible contributor.
  • Issues are typically closed automatically by GitHub when a Pull Request addressing them is merged, at which point they are moved to the "Done" column.
  • At the start of each month, a new column is created for the previous month, and all issues from the "Done" column are manually moved into it to maintain historical records.

Our project dashboard follows a monthly archival pattern, moving closed issues to their respective month columns:

  • October 25
  • September 25

Apart from documentation, another way to get involved with the project is with Project Management. For example, we need users of the Platform to discover and report bugs in the project. We need volunteers to report on the issue board and respond to new issues from the Community. Reproducing issues or responding to the issues with request for additional information to aid in reproduction of the issue are incredibly valuable ways to contribute to the project.

docs.title: Commit Practice
docs.text:
We recommend using commit prefixes to make changes clear at a glance. Each commit should include a description explaining the intention and context of the change to support future development and historical reference.

  • :doctype - changes related to frappe doctype and their rationale
  • :backend - backend code modifications supplying data to the site
  • :frontend - changes to web pages and user interface
  • :fix - corrections for broken functionality, referencing the cause
  • :minor - minor or maintenance updates with no functional impact
  • :init - initial setup or boilerplate for new features
  • :feat - completed feature implementations
  • :test - updates or additions to unit tests
  • :dashboard - modifications to dashboard components

docs.title: Reviewing proposals
docs.text:
Usually, after the proposal submissions are closed for an event, the volunteers begin following up with reviewers to comment on the proposals. The FOSS United Community has a distributed team of volunteer reviewers. The distributed nature of the reviewers is an effort to prevent the chapter volunteers from favoring some proposers over others and to improve transparency in the decision making process.

Reviewing community proposals is a hard job and it becomes especially hard if you want to provide meaningful feedback to the proposers to enable them to improve the proposals. Effectively reviewing proposals is a learned skill and if you have experience writing and reviewing proposals, and you are interested in volunteering with the FOSS United Community, please reach out to the Foundation.

Once you're added as a reviewer, you should be able to see a new "Review Proposals" page on the Dashboard.

docs.title: Submitting a review
docs.text:
• Click on one of the events listed in the "Review Proposals" page to see the list of submitted proposals
  • Click on one of the proposals to see detailed information about the proposal and to submit a proposal

Note: We humbly request the reviewers to provide constructive criticism of the proposals. One word reviews are strongly discouraged. Almost all proposals can be improved in some way or another and it is the reviewers' responsibility to provide this necessary feedback to the proposers. There exists an equilibrium between the proposers and the reviewers - if the reviewers are unnecessarily harsh, proposers become demotivated over time and the likelihood of repeat proposals from the same proposer goes down. However, if the reviewers approve all proposals without providing meaningful feedback, the proposers don't have any incentive to improve their proposals over time, also leading to fewer sound proposals. The long-term quality of proposals and talks in the FOSS United Community depends on the reviewers.

docs.title: Updating a review
docs.text: • Reviews can be updated by clicking on the "Edit Review" button on the proposal

docs.title: What is RSS
docs.text: RSS (Really Simple Syndication or Rich Site Summary) is a web feed format used to publish frequently updated content like blog posts, news headlines, podcasts, or articles in a standardized way. It allows users to subscribe to content from multiple sources and receive updates automatically in an RSS reader or aggregator, without needing to visit each site individually. RSS is a common tool for keeping up with information posted to your favorite sites.

docs.title: Importance of RSS for FOSS (Free and Open Source Software)
docs.text:
1. Decentralization & Control

    RSS supports open, decentralized content distribution, aligning with FOSS values. Users control what they follow no algorithms, ads, or manipulation.

  2. Privacy-Respecting

    RSS does not track users or collect personal data. Unlike social media, it's a privacy-friendly way to stay updated.

  3. Transparency & Openness

    RSS feeds are open standards able to inspect, modify, and implement, encouraging transparency and interoperability.

  4. Freedom from Platforms

    FOSS communities often value freedom from corporate platforms. RSS allows users to consume and share content independently of centralized services like Twitter or Facebook.

  5. Promoting Independent Projects

    Many FOSS projects use RSS to announce releases, blog posts, or updates. It's a simple way to broadcast updates to interested users without needing a proprietary communication channel.

docs.title: Marketing Events on Social Media
docs.text: Promoting events effectively is key to growing the FOSS community and raising awareness about Free and Open Source Software. Every FOSS United event should be announced across our communication channels, including the FOSS United Forum and social media platforms.

docs.title: Pre-Event Promotion
docs.text:
Before each event, make sure to share:

  • Talk posters (if available)
  • Event schedule
  • Agenda and speaker information

While posters are not mandatory, sharing event details, with or without visuals, is essential. Social media helps amplify our mission, spread awareness of open source, and invite broader participation from the community.

docs.title: Using Design Templates
docs.text:
When creating visual content such as posters or banners, follow the official FOSS United branding guidelines:

  • Use standard FOSS United templates, color schemes, and fonts
  • Refer to the FOSS United Chennai team's design templates for examples and inspiration

Maintaining a consistent design style helps establish a recognizable identity for all FOSS United chapters and events.

docs.title: Where to Share and Engage
docs.text: To maximize visibility and reach, share event details across the following platforms:

docs.title: 2. Telegram Groups

Most real-time conversations happen in the FOSS United Telegram group. We have a dedicated Telegram groups for each city chapter, listed on telegram page.

This telegram group is also bridged with out matrix server

docs.title: 3. Social Media Channels
docs.text:
Use our official social media accounts to promote events and updates. Tag these accounts when sharing content:

  • Twitter
  • LinkedIn
  • Instagram
  • Mastodon
  • Bluesky
  • Reddit

Content can include event announcements, speaker highlights, schedules, reminders, and post-event summaries.

docs.title: 4. Newsletters and Mailing Lists
docs.text: Encourage people to subscribe to our newsletter to receive updates, announcements, and invitations to future events.

docs.title: 5. Events Page and Timeline
docs.text:
Ensure the event is listed on the official Events Timeline. This allows the wider community to discover and register for upcoming meetups, conferences, and hackathons.

By promoting events across these channels, you help increase awareness of FOSS, support community engagement, and contribute to the ongoing growth of FOSS United across India.

docs.title: Speaking at FOSS Events
docs.text: Speaking at FOSS United events provides a unique platform for individuals to share their knowledge, insights, and experiences with a diverse and engaged audience. Here are some of the opportunities and benefits associated with speaking at FOSS United events:

docs.title: Opportunities:
docs.text:
1. Presenting Talks: Share your expertise on a specific topic, technology, or project related to open-source software.
  2. Panel Discussions: Participate in panel discussions with other experts, engaging in lively debates and sharing diverse perspectives.
  3. Workshops and Tutorials: Lead hands-on workshops or tutorials, providing practical knowledge and skills to attendees.
  4. Keynote Speeches: Opportunity to deliver keynote speeches, setting the tone for the event and inspiring the audience.
  5. Community Engagement: Engage with the community through Q&A sessions, meet-and-greets, and informal discussions.
  6. Collaborative Projects: Showcase collaborative projects and initiatives, highlighting the power of community-driven development.

docs.title: Benefits:
docs.text:
1. Professional Recognition: Gain recognition as an expert in your field, enhancing your professional credibility and reputation.
  2. Networking: Connect to other professionals, industry leaders, and enthusiasts in the open-source community.
  3. Skill Enhancement: Improve your public speaking, presentation, and leadership skills through real-world experience.
  4. Knowledge Sharing: Contribute to the collective knowledge of the community by sharing your insights, research, and experiences.
  5. Influence and Impact: Influence the direction of the open-source movement and make a positive impact on the community.
  6. Collaboration Opportunities: Forge new collaborations and partnerships with like-minded individuals and organizations.
  7. Personal Growth: Experience personal growth and fulfillment by contributing to a cause you are passionate about.
  8. Access to Exclusive Content: Enjoy access to exclusive content, workshops, and sessions at the event.
  9. Promote Your Work: A platform to promote your work, projects, or products to a targeted audience.
  10. Cultural Exchange: Engage with a diverse audience, fostering cultural understanding and the exchange of ideas.
  11. Feedback and Insights: Receive valuable feedback and insights from peers and experts, helping you grow and refine your ideas.
  12. Supportive Environment: Present in a supportive and encouraging environment that values collaboration and community.

FOSS United provides clear guidelines for talk proposals, ensuring a transparent and fair selection process. Whether you are an experienced speaker or looking to make your debut, FOSS United events offer a welcoming platform to share, learn, connect, and grow. It's an opportunity to be part of a vibrant community that celebrates open-source culture and innovation.

docs.title: Perks of Volunteering
docs.text:
Volunteering at FOSS United offers a multitude of benefits that can enrich both personal and professional growth. Here are some of the key advantages:

  1. Skill Development: Enhance and develop new skills, whether in coding, design, event management, writing, or other areas. It's a great opportunity to learn and grow.

  2. Networking Opportunities: Connect to like-minded individuals, industry experts, and professionals in the open-source community. Build valuable relationships and expand your network.

  3. Contribute to Meaningful Projects: Work on projects that align with your passions and interests. Your contributions can have a real impact on the community and the broader tech ecosystem.

  4. Professional Recognition: Gain recognition for your work and build a portfolio that showcases your contributions. It can enhance your professional standing and open doors to new opportunities.

  5. Personal Fulfillment: Experience the satisfaction of contributing to a cause you believe in. Volunteering can provide a sense of purpose and fulfillment.

  6. Collaborative Environment: Work in a collaborative and supportive environment where ideas are shared, and creativity is encouraged.

  7. Influence and Leadership: Take on leadership roles, influence the direction of projects, and make decisions that shape the future of the community.

  8. Educational Opportunities: Access educational resources, workshops, and mentorship opportunities that can further your knowledge and expertise.

  9. Flexibility: Choose how and when you contribute. Whether you have a few hours a week or want to engage more deeply, there's flexibility to match your availability.

  10. Promote Open Source Culture: Play a part in promoting and sustaining the open-source culture, which emphasizes collaboration, transparency, and community-driven development.

  11. Build a Positive Reputation: By adhering to community guidelines and contributing positively, you can build a reputation as a responsible and respected member of the community.

  12. Potential Career Advancement: For those looking to build a career in technology, volunteering with FOSS United can provide valuable experience and connections that may lead to job opportunities.

  13. Civic Engagement: Participate in public policy advocacy and civic engagement to shape laws and regulations that affect the open-source community.

  14. Cultural Exchange: Engage with a diverse community, fostering cultural understanding and exchange of ideas.

docs.title: Volunteering in the FOSS United Community
docs.text: Volunteers are the backbone of the FOSS United community. While the FOSS United Foundation has a small core team, it's the energy and dedication of hundreds of volunteers across the country that bring our initiatives, events, and programs to life.

docs.title: Why Volunteer?
docs.text:
Volunteering at FOSS United offers an opportunity to:

  • Contribute to the open-source movement in India
  • Learn and grow alongside like-minded individuals
  • Develop leadership and organizational skills
  • Build a network with contributors, developers, and professionals from across the country

Read more on perks of volunteering.

However, volunteering is a serious commitment. Many active volunteers contribute 10–20 hours (or more) each month. Volunteers are held to a higher standard within the community because of their role in shaping and sustaining it.

docs.title: What Do Volunteers Do?
docs.text:
Volunteers are involved in many aspects of running FOSS United activities. Some typical responsibilities include:

  • Organizing and promoting events (meetups, conferences, hackathons)
  • Finding venues, handling logistics, and managing operations on the ground
  • Putting out calls for proposals and coordinating with speakers
  • Engaging with attendees and gathering feedback
  • Designing posters, banners, and other creative assets
  • Promoting events and initiatives on social media
  • Reporting what went well and areas for improvement

docs.title: Volunteering Roles and Opportunities
docs.text:
Volunteers can contribute in a wide variety of ways. Here are some of the main areas where your skills and time can make an impact:

  1. Event Organization Help plan and execute events such as FOSS Hack, IndiaFOSS, and local meetups.

  2. Community Engagement Participate in discussions on the FOSS United Forum, answer questions, welcome new members, and keep the community active and welcoming.

  3. Design and Creativity Create visual assets like posters, logos, slide decks, or social media graphics using standard templates and FOSS United branding. Refer to the design templates by the Chennai team for inspiration.

  4. Marketing and Outreach Help promote events, write blog posts, manage newsletters, and grow the community on platforms like Twitter, LinkedIn, and Instagram.

  5. Educational Programs Contribute to initiatives like FOSS Clubs and Mon School through mentoring, content creation, or coordination.

  6. Public Policy and Advocacy Support our work on open-source policy, government engagement, and research.

  7. Fundraising and Financial Support Assist in sponsorship efforts, donor communications, or event budgeting.

  8. Companies can join as industry partners

  9. Individuals can donate any amount (donations are eligible for 80G and CSR tax benefits)

  10. Code Contributions Developers can contribute code to projects supported by FOSS United or help maintain tools used by the community.

  11. Join Specialized Teams Depending on your interests, join focused groups working on policy, education, tech infrastructure, or community development.

  12. Propose Your Own Contribution Have a unique skill or project idea? We’re open to custom contributions that align with our mission.

docs.title: Join a City Chapter
docs.text:
If you're interested in volunteering with a local chapter:

  • Reach out to existing volunteers from the chapter
  • If you're already a chapter volunteer, you can add others via the "Members" tab on the Dashboard

docs.title: Start or Restart a Chapter or Club
docs.text: Interested in starting a new city chapter or reviving an existing one? Want to set up a FOSS Club at your educational institution? Reach out to the FOSS United Foundation team directly.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: Once you're on-boarded as a volunteer, the Dashboard becomes your central tool to manage tasks, events, members, and chapters.

docs.title: Chapter Management
docs.text: Manage city-specific tasks, track event planning, and collaborate with other volunteers from the Manage Chapter section.

docs.title: Learn More
docs.text:
To explore current volunteering opportunities and responsibilities in detail, check out this forum thread: Draft: Tasks and Responsibilities Overview - FOSS United Foundation

Also, visit: How can I contribute to FOSS United?

Volunteering at FOSS United is a chance to be part of something bigger, to help build a sustainable, inclusive, and impacting open-source ecosystem in India. Whether you're a student, professional, designer, developer, or educator, there’s a place for you here.
